exits.notes: Employment ended 2019-01-18; he stopped acting as CFO on 2019-01-07 when Neumann started and stayed 'for a brief transition period' (d214). Reason as filed: the 2018-08-13 8-K says he 'intends to resign' (d212) and the press release that he 'plans to step down' (d213); the 2020 proxy calls it a 'mutually agreed departure' and says he signed Netflix's standard release agreement (d202). Severance: $4,500,000 lump sum 'calculated in accordance with the Severance Plan' (nine months of allocatable compensation, d208), in FY2019 All Other Compensation (d203, d204); it equals the 2019 proxy's Potential Payments estimate (d211). No accelerated equity: officers' monthly options were fully vested at grant (d209); null because no filing quantifies it. No consulting or other exit pay disclosed (null); the 2019 401(k) match ($4,711) and tax preparation ($1,511) are ordinary benefits, not exit pay. 2019 salary was prorated to the end date. total_exit_pay = the plain sum of recorded components (severance only).

Employment ended 2019-06-30 (d201). Reason as filed: on 2019-03-07 the company announced he 'intends to resign as Chief Marketing Officer pending the appointment of his replacement' (d210); the 2020 proxy calls it a 'mutually agreed departure' with Netflix's standard release agreement (d202). No 8-K was filed for his departure. Severance: $5,250,000 lump sum under the Severance Plan (nine months of his $7,000,000 allocatable compensation), in FY2019 All Other Compensation (d205, d206); it equals the 2019 proxy's Potential Payments estimate (d211). 2019 salary was prorated to his end date (d207). No accelerated equity (options fully vested at grant, d209; null because not quantified). No consulting or other exit pay disclosed (null); 401(k) match ($9,800), tax preparation ($1,481) and car services ($25,818) in the same footnote are ordinary perquisites. total_exit_pay = the plain sum of recorded components (severance only).

Not a departure from the company: on 2025-04-11 he 'informed the Company of his intent to transition from his executive officer position' and from 2025-04-17 served as non-executive Chairman (d220); the 2026 proxy describes it as 'part of the natural evolution of our leadership structure and executive planning' (d222). His employment ended then. The 2026 proxy states he 'did not receive any severance' (d221, d223), so severance_cash = 0. Equity was forfeited, not accelerated: all 8,610 unvested PSUs and 7,710 unvested RSUs (about $827,963 and $741,417 at the 2025-04-16 close) plus his 2025 bonus opportunity (d222), so accelerated_equity_value = 0. No consulting or other exit pay is disclosed (null). After the transition he received director stock options from May 2025 under the Director Equity Compensation Plan, reported in the SCT as 2025 Option Awards of $271,234 (d224, d225, d307) - board pay, not exit pay, and not in the Director Compensation table. He left the Board at the 2026-06-04 annual meeting (did not stand; board file); no payment on that is disclosed. Earlier title changes (CEO to co-CEO 2020-07-14, co-CEO/President to Executive Chairman 2023-01-13) kept him an employee and executive officer and are not exits. total_exit_pay = the plain sum of recorded components (0 + 0).

Not a departure: she stopped being a Rule 3b-7 executive officer after 2023-01-13, when the Board re-determined the executive officers (d233), and 'remain[s] employed at the Company' as Chief Communications Officer (d230, d231, d234). No separation payment or agreement is disclosed, so all components are null. The 2024 proxy's Potential Payments table shows a hypothetical $6,750,000 termination/change-in-control amount as of 2023-12-31 (d232); it was not triggered and is not recorded as exit pay. No later filing reports her leaving Netflix (she is no longer a Section 16 filer; last Form 4 2023-01-04).

Not a departure: he stopped being a Rule 3b-7 executive officer after 2023-01-13 (d233) and 'remain[s] employed at the Company' as Chief Talent Officer (d230, d231, d235). No separation payment or agreement is disclosed, so all components are null. The 2024 proxy's Potential Payments table shows a hypothetical $6,500,000 termination/change-in-control amount as of 2023-12-31 (d232); it was not triggered and is not recorded as exit pay. No later filing reports him leaving Netflix (no longer a Section 16 filer; last Form 4 2023-01-04).

coverage.method: Director Compensation tables from all eight definitive proxies filed 2019-2026 (DEF 14A each year; no DEFC14A/DEFR14A, and the only 10-K/A, filed 2019-02-08, is exhibit-only). One row per (filing, listed director): 11 rows per year for FY2018, 10 for FY2019, 11 for FY2020-FY2021, 10 for FY2022-FY2024 and 11 for FY2025. Employee directors (Hastings, Sarandos, Peters) are excluded by the tables themselves; Hastings' FY2025 non-executive director options are in the SCT only. The 2022 PRE 14A and DEFA14A supplements are not recorded separately.

Every NEO in nflx_exec_comp_research.json whose executive-officer tenure ended: Wells (2019), Bennett (2019), Whetstone and Ezama (ceased being officers 2023-01-13, still employed) and Hastings (Executive Chairman to non-executive Chairman 2025-04-17). Sources: 2019, 2020, 2024 and 2026 proxies (CD&A, SCT All Other Compensation footnotes, Potential Payments sections), the 2018-08-13 and 2019-01-07 8-Ks (plus the 2018 press release exhibit) and the 2025-04-17 8-K. Title changes that kept the person an executive officer (Sarandos, Peters, Hyman, Hastings in 2020 and 2023) are not exits. No separation agreement exhibit was filed for any of them.
